pat.duty-on-one-link-in-a-chain.fix: Extend the duty to controlling persons and intermediaries, or add a rule making them answerable for evasion.
pat.election-into-a-lighter-parallel-reg: A party can register or qualify under a second statute with lighter duties.
Find other statutes under which a party could register or qualify with lighter duties. Ask whether this bill addresses that choice.
State which regime governs when more than one applies, and bar election into the lighter one for the same activity.
pat.timing-moves-around-a-date.plain: Parties shift transactions across an effective date or holding period.
pat.timing-moves-around-a-date.check: Find effective dates and holding periods. Ask whether transactions could be moved across them, and whether a look back or anti-timing rule exists.
pat.timing-moves-around-a-date.fix: Add a look back period and a rule disregarding transactions timed mainly to fall on the favorable side of a date.
pat.netting-that-cancels-a-charge.plain: Offset rules let a new tax or duty be reduced toward zero.
pat.netting-that-cancels-a-charge.check: Find offset, credit and netting rules attached to a new charge or duty. Ask whether they could reduce it toward zero.
pat.netting-that-cancels-a-charge.fix: Cap offsets, or provide a minimum amount that cannot be netted away.
pat.offsetting-response-by-another-gover: A state or other government can redesign its own law to neutralize the federal limit.
Find limits placed on another level of government. Ask whether it could redesign its own law to neutralize the limit, and whether the text anticipates that.
Add a rule addressing offsetting changes by other governments, and a reporting duty to track them.
pat.single-enforcer.plain: Only one federal agency may enforce, with no parallel authority for state attorneys general.
pat.single-enforcer.check: Find who may enforce. Ask whether state officials or others have parallel authority, and what happens if the one enforcer does not act.
pat.single-enforcer.fix: Give parallel enforcement authority to state officials and allow a private right of action as a backstop.
pat.no-reward-for-insiders.plain: The bill at most protects whistleblowers and offers no relator suit or bounty.
pat.no-reward-for-insiders.check: Look for protection, rewards or suit rights for insiders who report violations. Ask whether reporting carries any benefit beyond protection from retaliation.
pat.no-reward-for-insiders.fix: Add an insider reporting right with a share of recoveries, and protection from retaliation.
pat.private-right-without-economics.plai: A right to sue exists without statutory or multiplied damages or fee shifting, so small claims are not worth bringing.
pat.private-right-without-economics.chec: Find any right to sue and read the remedies. Ask whether damages, multiples or fee shifting make a small claim worth bringing.
pat.private-right-without-economics.fix: Add statutory or multiplied damages and shifting of reasonable fees to a prevailing plaintiff.
pat.fees-lost-on-voluntary-compliance.pl: Fee shifting applies only to judgments, so a defendant can comply after suit and avoid fees.
pat.fees-lost-on-voluntary-compliance.ch: Read the fee shifting terms. Ask whether fees are available only after a judgment, and whether a defendant could comply after suit and avoid them.
pat.fees-lost-on-voluntary-compliance.fi: Allow fees where the suit prompted the change in conduct, not only after judgment.
pat.non-enforcement-left-unreviewable.pl: No standards or triggers say when the agency must enforce, so a decision not to enforce, including for a whole category, cannot be challenged.
pat.non-enforcement-left-unreviewable.ch: Find standards for when the agency must enforce. Ask whether a decision not to enforce, including for a whole category, can be challenged.
pat.non-enforcement-left-unreviewable.fi: State criteria or triggers for enforcement and allow review of a refusal to enforce, with a reporting duty.
pat.statutory-damages-without-concrete-h: Fixed damages for a bare violation leave many plaintiffs without standing in federal court.
Find fixed damages for a bare violation. Ask whether a plaintiff must show concrete harm to sue in federal court, and which plaintiffs would be left out.
Define the injury the provision addresses, allow other enforcers to sue, and provide an alternative forum.
pat.agency-penalties-without-a-court-pat: Civil penalties can be imposed only in the agency's own tribunal, which is open to a jury-trial challenge.
Find civil penalties imposed in the agency's own tribunal. Ask whether a court route exists, and whether a jury trial challenge could stall them.
Provide a court action for penalties as an alternative to the agency tribunal.
pat.funding-conditions-without-rights-la: Duties are written as conditions on grants without clear rights-creating terms, so beneficiaries cannot sue.
Find duties written as conditions on grants. Ask whether the text uses clear rights creating language, and whether beneficiaries could sue.
Use express rights creating language and state who may enforce it.
pat.independence-resting-on-removal-prot: The design assumes enforcers cannot be removed at will.
Find protections that assume enforcers cannot be removed at will. Ask what happens to the design if a court finds those protections invalid.
Add a fallback structure that keeps the body's function if removal protection is invalidated.
pat.missing-clear-statement-on-states.pl: The bill alters the federal-state balance or subjects states to suit without the explicit statement courts require.
pat.missing-clear-statement-on-states.ch: Find provisions that change the federal and state balance or subject states to suit. Ask whether the text says so explicitly in the way courts require.
pat.missing-clear-statement-on-states.fi: State the intended effect on state governments in clear express terms.
pat.mental-state-unstated-or-set-high.pl: A penalty provision is silent on mental state, or liability attaches only to "willful" or "knowing" violations.
pat.mental-state-unstated-or-set-high.ch: Find penalty provisions and read the mental state required. Ask whether it is unstated, or limited to 'willful' or 'knowing' acts, and what a regulated party could claim not to know.
pat.mental-state-unstated-or-set-high.fi: State the required mental state and provide for civil liability without proof of intent.
pat.ambiguity-in-a-penalty-provision.pla: Unclear words in a provision carrying criminal penalties are read for the defendant, and that reading can carry into civil cases.
pat.ambiguity-in-a-penalty-provision.che: Find unclear words in provisions carrying criminal penalties. Ask whether the narrower reading would be applied, and whether that reading could carry into civil cases.
pat.ambiguity-in-a-penalty-provision.fix: Define the key terms of any penalty provision and separate the civil standard from the criminal one.
pat.narrowing-by-constitutional-doubt.pl: A party can win a narrow reading by raising a serious constitutional question without winning the constitutional claim.
pat.narrowing-by-constitutional-doubt.ch: Find provisions that could raise a serious constitutional question. Ask whether a court could adopt a narrow reading to avoid it.
pat.narrowing-by-constitutional-doubt.fi: Include a clear statement of intended breadth and findings supporting the provision.
pat.gates-on-private-suits.plain: A mandatory notice period, a bar when the government is "diligently prosecuting", or a government power to dismiss lets a suit be headed off.
pat.gates-on-private-suits.check: Find notice periods, bars during government prosecution and government powers to dismiss. Ask whether a suit could be headed off by them.
pat.gates-on-private-suits.fix: Limit the notice period, define when a government action blocks a suit, and require court approval of dismissals.
pat.private-relator-open-to-challenge.pl: Enforcement by relators on the government's behalf faces unresolved Article II objections.
pat.private-relator-open-to-challenge.ch: Find enforcement by private parties on the government's behalf. Ask what constitutional objections could be raised and what happens if they succeed.
pat.private-relator-open-to-challenge.fi: Add a government enforcement path that continues if the relator mechanism is invalidated.
pat.past-violations-not-actionable.plain: Private suits reach only ongoing or future violations, or only forward-looking relief.
pat.past-violations-not-actionable.check: Read what private suits may reach. Ask whether past violations can be sued over or only ongoing ones, and whether only forward looking relief is available.
pat.past-violations-not-actionable.fix: Allow suit over past violations within a stated period and provide for damages as well as forward looking relief.
pat.limitation-period-that-never-restart: The period runs from the first act and does not restart with each continuing effect.
Find limitation periods and their start points. Ask whether each continuing effect restarts the clock or only the first act counts.
State that each continuing violation or new effect starts a new period.
pat.no-time-limit-on-rule-challenges.pla: The bill relies on the general six-year limit, which restarts for each newly injured party.
pat.no-time-limit-on-rule-challenges.che: Look for a time limit on challenges to rules made under the bill. Ask whether the general default period applies and when it restarts.
pat.no-time-limit-on-rule-challenges.fix: State a specific filing period for challenges and when it starts.
pat.filing-rule-readable-as-jurisdiction: A deadline or precondition is worded so that a court treats it as a limit on its power, not a waivable rule.
Find deadlines and preconditions to suit. Ask whether the wording could be read as a limit on the court's power instead of a waivable rule.
Word deadlines as claim processing rules and state that they may be waived or tolled.
pat.private-trigger-open-to-misuse.plain: A private notice or complaint compels action with no penalty for false notices, no counter-notice and too little time to verify.
pat.private-trigger-open-to-misuse.check: Find private notices or complaints that compel action. Ask what penalizes false ones, whether a counter notice exists, and whether time to verify is enough.
pat.private-trigger-open-to-misuse.fix: Add a penalty for false notices, a counter notice process and a reasonable verification period.
pat.enforcement-gated-by-a-vote-or-limit: A penalty requires a political vote before it applies, or recovery is limited to realized profit.
Find penalties that need a vote before they apply, or recovery limited to realized profit. Ask who controls the vote and whether the cap makes violation cheap.
Remove the vote requirement and allow recovery beyond profit, such as damages or fixed penalties.
pat.dollar-figures-not-indexed.plain: Penalties, caps and thresholds are fixed nominal amounts that erode or drift with inflation.
pat.dollar-figures-not-indexed.check: List each fixed dollar penalty, cap and threshold. Ask whether it is indexed, and what it will be worth after several years of inflation.
pat.dollar-figures-not-indexed.fix: Index dollar figures to a named measure with a scheduled adjustment.
pat.penalties-deductible-or-untracked.pl: Nothing bars deducting penalties or directs where penalty money goes.
pat.penalties-deductible-or-untracked.ch: Find the treatment of penalty payments. Ask whether they can be deducted or recovered from others, and where the money goes.
pat.penalties-deductible-or-untracked.fi: Bar deduction of penalties and direct where penalty receipts are deposited and reported.
pat.appropriated-funds-can-be-withheld.p: Money is appropriated but nothing forces timely obligation or lets anyone sue if it is held back.
pat.appropriated-funds-can-be-withheld.c: Find appropriations and ask whether anything forces timely obligation. Ask whether anyone can sue if the money is held back.
pat.appropriated-funds-can-be-withheld.f: Add a deadline for obligating funds and a reporting duty on delays.
pat.funding-that-depends-on-a-request.pl: Mandatory funding flows only when the agency head asks or a contested formula term is met.
pat.funding-that-depends-on-a-request.ch: Find funding that flows only on a request or a formula term. Ask who controls the request, and what happens if no one makes it.
pat.funding-that-depends-on-a-request.fi: Provide funding by default, with the request or formula as an adjustment rather than a condition.
pat.offsets-that-score-without-changing-: Changes in mandatory programs, or the repeated delay of a rule never in force, are counted as savings.
Find savings used to pay for new spending. Ask whether they change actual outlays, or count the delay of a rule never in force.
Report the savings and the basis for scoring them, and require a review of actual outlays.
pat.designations-and-timing-shifts-outsi: Emergency designations, advance appropriations and timing shifts take spending outside budget limits.
Find emergency designations, advance appropriations and timing shifts. Ask whether they move spending outside budget limits.
Require a stated justification for each designation and report totals against the limits.
pat.spending-authority-outside-appropria: Contract or borrowing authority commits funds without an appropriation.
Find contract or borrowing authority. Ask whether it commits funds without an appropriation, and who reviews the commitments.
Require appropriation or a reporting and review step before any commitment is made.
pat.provision-shaped-to-a-reconciliation: A provision is sized, sunset or worded to survive the Byrd rule.
Find provisions sized, dated or worded to meet a special budget procedure. Ask whether the form departs from what the policy would otherwise need.
Disclose which provisions were shaped for the procedure and review them after enactment.
pat.serial-short-term-renewal.plain: Temporary provisions are renewed repeatedly instead of being made permanent or ended.
pat.serial-short-term-renewal.check: Find temporary provisions and their expiry dates. Ask whether they have been renewed before, and whether making them permanent or ending them is an option.
pat.serial-short-term-renewal.fix: Set a longer term or a review that leads to a permanent or terminal decision.
pat.mandate-silent-on-who-pays.plain: A requirement is imposed without saying which party bears its cost.
pat.mandate-silent-on-who-pays.check: Find each requirement and ask which party bears its cost. Ask whether the text says, and what happens if that party cannot pay.
pat.mandate-silent-on-who-pays.fix: State who bears the cost and how, with funding or cost sharing where needed.
Two programs pay for the same period or need with no coordination clause.
Find programs that pay for the same period or need. Ask whether a clause coordinates them, and whether double payment is possible.
Add a coordination clause providing for offset or priority between the programs.
pat.amendatory-instruction-that-cannot-b: A strike, insert or redesignation instruction is ambiguous or does not match the text it amends.
Check each strike, insert and redesignation instruction against the text it amends. Ask whether it can be carried out exactly as written.
Verify each instruction against the current text of the amended law before enactment.
pat.reference-inside-amendatory-text-to-: Inside quoted text, "this Act" or "the date of enactment of this Act" refers to the amended statute, not the new bill.
Read quoted inserted text for 'this Act' and 'date of enactment of this Act'. Ask whether it points to the amended law or the new bill.
Name the intended law and date expressly inside the inserted text.
A bill amends the Code for a non-positive-law title, or the Act for a positive-law title.
Check whether each amendment targets the Code or the Act, and whether the title is positive law. Ask whether the citation form fits.
Use the correct citation form for each title and confirm it with the codifiers.
pat.broken-circular-or-chained-cross-ref: A reference points to the wrong unit, to itself, or through a series of other references.
Follow each cross-reference to its target. Ask whether it points to the right unit, to itself, or through a chain of other references.
Replace chained references with direct ones and check that each target exists.
pat.repeal-or-sunset-with-unintended-sur: A repeal does not revive prior law, and a sunset of authority leaves the Act's amendments in force.
Read each repeal and sunset. Ask whether prior law returns, and whether amendments made by the Act stay in force after the authority ends.
State which provisions and amendments end, and whether earlier law is restored.
pat.repeal-silent-on-accrued-liabilities: A repeal or expiry does not say whether penalties already incurred survive, leaving the general savings statute to decide.
Read each repeal or expiry for penalties already incurred. Ask whether they survive or the general savings rule decides.
State whether accrued penalties and pending cases continue after repeal or expiry.
pat.effective-date-confused-with-applica: The date text takes effect is not distinguished from the persons, things or events it applies to.
Find each effective date. Ask whether the text separates the date it takes effect from the persons, things and events it applies to.
State the effective date and the applicability rule in separate provisions.
pat.no-transitional-rules.plain: The bill changes current programs or behavior without saying how existing cases move to the new rule.
pat.no-transitional-rules.check: Look for rules on how existing cases, contracts and programs move to the new rule. Ask what happens to those in progress on the effective date.
pat.no-transitional-rules.fix: Add transitional provisions covering pending matters and a schedule for existing cases.
pat.substantive-rule-stranded-in-an-amen: A free-standing rule sits in an amending or temporary section where it will not be codified with the parent law.
Find free standing rules in amending or temporary sections. Ask whether they will be codified with the parent law and found by readers.
Place the rule in the parent law or state how it is to be codified.
pat.restatement-of-other-law.plain: A provision repeats existing law, creating two sources that can diverge.
pat.restatement-of-other-law.check: Find provisions repeating existing law. Ask whether the two sources could diverge, and which one governs if they do.
pat.restatement-of-other-law.fix: Cross-refer to the existing law instead of restating it, or state which text governs.
pat.conflict-with-international-obligati: The measure collides with a treaty or trade commitment, which general override language does not reach.
Compare the measure with treaty and trade commitments. Ask whether any conflict exists, and whether general override language reaches it.
Add an express statement on the relationship to those obligations and a review step.
pat.boilerplate-relied-on-for-work-it-do: Stock phrases such as a general override or a routine severability clause are treated as protective.
Find stock clauses such as a general override or severability. Ask whether they actually protect what the drafters think they protect.
Replace boilerplate with specific text where protection matters, such as named provisions or tailored severability.
pat.no-protection-from-later-implied-ove: Nothing requires a later law to refer to this one expressly before displacing it.
Look for any rule that a later law must refer to this one expressly to displace it. Ask whether a later law could override it silently.
Add a clause requiring express reference by any later law that would displace this one.
pat.no-fallback-if-struck-down.plain: No substitute rule takes effect if a court invalidates the primary provision.
pat.no-fallback-if-struck-down.check: Find the primary provision and ask what applies if a court invalidates it. Ask whether any substitute takes effect.
pat.no-fallback-if-struck-down.fix: Add a fallback rule that takes effect if the primary provision is invalidated.
Provisions enacted as a package are not made inseverable, so a court can remove one side of the bargain.
Find provisions enacted as a package or bargain. Ask whether the text makes them inseverable, and what remains if a court removes one side.
State which provisions stand or fall together and add a fallback.
pat.no-fast-track-for-validity-challenge: Constitutional challenges follow ordinary procedure, so the law's status stays uncertain for years.
Look for expedited procedure for constitutional challenges. Ask how long the law's status could stay uncertain under ordinary procedure.
Provide expedited review, a single forum and direct appeal for validity challenges.
pat.savings-clause-that-does-not-stop-im: A clause preserving state law does not prevent a finding of conflict preemption, and loose terms such as "requirements" sweep in common-law claims.
Read each clause preserving state law. Ask whether it stops a finding of conflict preemption, and whether words such as 'requirements' reach common law claims.
Add an express statement that conflict preemption does not apply to preserved state law, and define 'requirements'.
pat.preemption-without-a-replacement-sta: State rules are displaced while the federal level of regulation is left at zero.
Find provisions displacing state rules. Ask what federal standard fills the gap, and what level of regulation remains.
Pair displacement with a federal standard, or limit displacement to areas the federal rule covers.
pat.funding-conditions-that-deter-state-: Grant eligibility is used to discourage state or local regulation.
Find grant eligibility terms touching state or local regulation. Ask whether they discourage governments from adopting their own rules.
Limit conditions to the use of the funds and state that eligibility does not depend on forgoing state rules.
pat.no-anti-backsliding-rule.plain: Standards, permits or plans can be revised downward at renewal with no floor.
pat.no-anti-backsliding-rule.check: Find provisions for revising standards, permits or plans. Ask whether any floor prevents a downward revision at renewal.
pat.no-anti-backsliding-rule.fix: Add a rule that revisions may not be less protective than the existing standard without a stated finding.
pat.no-construction-rule-for-coverage.pl: No instruction says coverage terms are to be read broadly to serve the purpose.
pat.no-construction-rule-for-coverage.ch: Look for an instruction on how broadly coverage terms are to be read. Ask whether a narrow reading would defeat the stated purpose.
pat.no-construction-rule-for-coverage.fi: Add a rule that coverage terms are construed to serve the purpose, and state exceptions narrowly.
pat.later-ratification-of-a-lenient-read: Reenactment without change lets a party argue Congress accepted an agency's or court's narrow reading.
Find provisions reenacted without change after an agency or court read them narrowly. Ask whether a party could argue that the legislature accepted that reading.
State in the text that reenactment does not approve any prior reading.
pat.orphaned-functions-after-a-sunset.pl: The administering body expires while its contracts, licences or fee streams continue with no successor named.
pat.orphaned-functions-after-a-sunset.ch: Find bodies that expire and ask what happens to their contracts, licenses and fee streams. Ask whether a successor is named.
pat.orphaned-functions-after-a-sunset.fi: Name a successor body and provide for transfer of functions when an agency sunsets.
pat.no-authority-to-correct-a-known-flaw: The agency cannot fix an acknowledged error or distortion without new legislation.
Look for authority to fix an acknowledged error without new legislation. Ask what the agency could do if a flaw appears.
Add a limited correction authority with notice, a stated finding and a reporting duty.
pat.eligibility-by-self-attestation.plai: A benefit or status is established by the applicant's own statement, with verification barred or not required.
pat.eligibility-by-self-attestation.chec: Find benefits or status established by the applicant's own statement. Ask whether verification is allowed, barred or required.
pat.eligibility-by-self-attestation.fix: Allow after the fact verification and audit of attestations, with penalties for false statements.
pat.bar-on-sharing-data-between-agencies: A statute's wording or silence stops one agency from giving another the data it needs.
Read confidentiality and privacy language. Ask whether it stops one agency from giving another the data it needs to carry out the bill.
Add an express data sharing authority with safeguards.
pat.decision-rule-decoupled-from-its-dri: A decision is separated in time from the choices that make it necessary, and inaction produces an outcome no one intends.
Find decisions set apart in time from the choices that make them necessary. Ask what happens if no one acts, and whether that result is intended.
Set a default outcome that matches the intended policy and require a decision before the default applies.
pat.no-backstop-for-delegated-implemente: States or other delegates carry out the program with no federal default if they do not.
Find programs carried out by states or other delegates. Ask what happens if a delegate does not act, and whether a default exists.
Provide a federal default or takeover if the delegate does not carry out the program.
pat.no-scheduled-review-of-standards.pla: Standards are set once and coverage shrinks as conditions change.
pat.no-scheduled-review-of-standards.che: Look for a review date for standards set in the bill. Ask whether coverage could shrink as conditions change.
pat.no-scheduled-review-of-standards.fix: Add a scheduled review with a duty to update and report.
pat.review-duty-with-a-built-in-exit.pla: A periodic review or report can be skipped on the agency's own determination.
pat.review-duty-with-a-built-in-exit.che: Find periodic reviews and reports. Ask whether the agency may skip them on its own determination.
pat.review-duty-with-a-built-in-exit.fix: Make the review mandatory and require a published reason for any extension.
pat.power-to-exempt-whole-classes.plain: An agency may exempt "any entity or class of entities" on a broad public-interest finding.
pat.power-to-exempt-whole-classes.check: Find powers to exempt 'any entity or class of entities'. Ask what criteria bound it, and what limits the number or size of the groups exempted.
pat.power-to-exempt-whole-classes.fix: Limit the exemption power by named criteria, time limits and public notice.
pat.unrecorded-waivers-and-exemptions.pl: Waivers are granted with no public record of how many or to whom.
pat.unrecorded-waivers-and-exemptions.ch: Look for a public record of waivers and exemptions. Ask whether anyone can learn how many were granted and to whom.
pat.unrecorded-waivers-and-exemptions.fi: Require a public register of each waiver and an annual report.
pat.narrowing-or-deferral-after-enactmen: Regulations under a general grant narrow the statute, or a later amendment postpones duties before they apply.
Find general grants of rulemaking power and amendment risk. Ask whether regulations could narrow the statute or a later law could postpone duties before they apply.
Set the core terms in the statute and add a reporting duty on any narrowing or deferral.
pat.agency-barred-from-supplying-a-defin: Congress blocks the agency from issuing the rule that would fill a gap.
Find limits on the agency's power to issue rules. Ask what gap results, and who fills it.
State the definition in the bill or allow a narrow rule to fill the gap.
A review body can only recommend, or an inspector can be removed without notice and reasons.
Find review bodies and inspectors. Ask whether they can only recommend, and whether removal needs notice and reasons.
Give the body binding follow up duties and require notice and reasons for removal.
pat.structural-checks-that-can-stall-the: Quorum or supermajority rules let unfilled seats halt the agency's work.
Find quorum and supermajority rules. Ask whether unfilled seats could halt the agency, and what the fallback is.
Add a fallback for the lack of a quorum and a deadline for filling seats.
pat.deadline-that-distorts-priorities.pl: A rigid deadline or automatic default forces action on one duty at the cost of rushed rules or neglect of others.
pat.deadline-that-distorts-priorities.ch: Find rigid deadlines and automatic defaults. Ask whether they could force action on one duty at the cost of rushed rules or neglect of others.
pat.deadline-that-distorts-priorities.fi: Set priorities among duties and allow a stated extension with reasons.
pat.many-independent-clearance-points.pl: Many separate sign-offs are required before anything happens.
pat.many-independent-clearance-points.ch: Count the separate sign offs before anything happens. Ask whether any one can block action, and whether a time limit applies to each.
pat.many-independent-clearance-points.fi: Reduce the number of approvals, set a time limit for each and add a default if one is missed.
pat.administrative-burden-on-beneficiari: Paperwork and friction keep eligible people from a right or benefit that exists on paper.
Walk through the steps a person must take to claim a right or benefit. Ask how much paperwork and delay is involved, and who bears the cost.
Simplify the process, allow automatic enrollment where possible and require reporting on take up.
No clause requires review against purpose or secures the data to do it, and any review is done by the implementing body.
Look for a clause requiring review against the stated purpose and data to do it. Ask who performs the review.
Add an independent evaluation duty with a data plan and a published report.
pat.powers-never-commenced-or-used.plain: Authority is granted and never brought into operation, with no duty to report why.
pat.powers-never-commenced-or-used.check: Find powers that need a start date or a first act. Ask whether any duty requires them to be brought into operation or reported on if not used.
pat.powers-never-commenced-or-used.fix: Add a commencement date and a duty to report why any power has not been used.
pat.reform-that-codifies-existing-practi: A new rule would have changed almost no past cases.
Compare the new rule with current practice. Ask how many past cases it would have changed.
Add a measurable change or a review of whether the rule alters practice.
pat.committee-review-bypassed.plain: Text passes under emergency or leadership procedure, or a draft is enacted without the expected cleanup stage.
pat.committee-review-bypassed.check: Check how the text moved through the process. Ask whether it passed under emergency or leadership procedure, and whether a cleanup stage was skipped.
pat.committee-review-bypassed.fix: Require committee review and a posting period before floor action, and a technical review of the final text.
pat.externally-drafted-or-model-text.pla: Bill text is drafted by, or copied closely from, an outside organization.
pat.externally-drafted-or-model-text.che: Compare the text with outside documents. Ask whether it was drafted by or copied from an outside organization, and whether that is disclosed.
pat.externally-drafted-or-model-text.fix: Require disclosure of outside drafters and a review of the text against the bill's purpose.
A board's or official's recommendation takes effect unless Congress acts to stop it.
Find recommendations that take effect unless the legislature acts. Ask who can stop them, how quickly, and what happens if no one does.
Require an affirmative approval step, or a clear window and procedure for disapproval.
pat.expedited-procedure-that-limits-amen: Fast-track rules restrict debate and amendment.
Find fast track procedures. Ask what debate and amendment they allow, and what changes could not be made.
Allow amendment and a minimum debate period, or limit fast track to defined cases.
pat.authority-to-skip-public-comment.pla: Rules can take effect before or without comment through good-cause, interim final or guidance routes.
pat.authority-to-skip-public-comment.che: Find routes that allow rules to take effect without comment, such as good cause or interim final rules. Ask what limits them.
pat.authority-to-skip-public-comment.fix: Limit skipping comment to stated circumstances, set a sunset on interim rules and require later notice and comment.
pat.no-comparative-print.plain: The bill is drafted so that no document shows how it changes existing law.
pat.no-comparative-print.check: Look for a document showing how the bill changes existing law. Ask whether readers can see the changes without assembling them.
pat.no-comparative-print.fix: Require a comparative print to be published before consideration.
pat.no-cost-or-regulatory-impact-stateme: The accompanying report lacks a cost estimate or regulatory impact evaluation.
Look for a cost estimate and a regulatory impact evaluation with the bill. Ask who prepared them and whether they cover the main provisions.
Require a cost estimate and impact evaluation before consideration.
pat.no-agency-technical-review.plain: The bill was drafted without technical assistance from the agency that will administer it.
pat.no-agency-technical-review.check: Look for technical assistance from the agency that will administer the bill. Ask whether the text was reviewed for workability.
pat.no-agency-technical-review.fix: Request and publish a technical review from the administering agency before enactment.
pat.provision-added-or-dropped-late.plai: A check, fix or shield is added to or removed from a must-pass vehicle late in the process.
pat.provision-added-or-dropped-late.chec: Compare earlier versions of the vehicle with the final text. Ask what was added or removed late, especially checks, fixes and shields.
pat.provision-added-or-dropped-late.fix: Require a posting period for late changes and a record of what was added or dropped.
pat.drafting-and-reading-conventions-dif: Drafters do not follow several canons that courts apply, so text is read in ways its authors did not expect.
Compare the drafting style with the canons courts apply. Ask where the text could be read in ways its authors did not expect.
Have the text reviewed against common interpretive canons and add construction rules where they differ.
pat.procedure-that-favors-a-constituency: Procedural rules give particular groups information, standing or veto points.
Read procedural rules for who receives information, standing or veto points. Ask whether a particular group gains an advantage.
Open procedural rights to affected parties generally and require public notice of key steps.
rules.inq.obligation.0: What has the obligated party actually done with this discretion, here or under the closest earlier law?
rules.inq.obligation.1: The official's own stated reading; instances where the power went unused or was used against the purpose; who was affected and how many
rules.inq.obligation.2: Agency court filings and guidance; GAO and inspector general reports; oversight letters; news investigations
rules.inq.definitions.0: Who or what sits just outside each defined or limiting term?
rules.inq.definitions.1: Specific entities, products, record types or people on each side of the line; existing statutory definitions that could be borrowed
rules.inq.definitions.2: U.S. Code definitions; agency rules; case law on the term; industry filings
rules.inq.actors.0: Who else holds the authority, the records or the capability, and are they bound?
rules.inq.actors.1: Agencies and components by name; contractors; levels of government; what each is documented to hold or do
rules.inq.actors.2: Agency records libraries and FOIA logs; GAO; committee letters; earlier statutes with wider scope
rules.inq.timing.0: What happened at this deadline, or at deadlines like it?
rules.inq.timing.1: Dates met and missed; what followed; who could act when the date passed
rules.inq.timing.2: Court dockets; the Unified Agenda; GAO deadline reviews; contemporaneous reporting
rules.inq.exceptions.0: Who has used this exception or one like it, how often, and for what?
rules.inq.exceptions.1: Invocations with counts and dates; the stated ground against the apparent use
rules.inq.exceptions.2: Transparency reports; inspector general audits; annual FOIA reports; litigation records
rules.inq.enforcement.0: What happened when someone tried to enforce this, or a provision built the same way?
rules.inq.enforcement.1: Cases, courts, holdings and dates; who had standing; which remedy was available and which was refused
rules.inq.enforcement.2: Dockets and opinions; Justice Department filings; enforcement records under parallel statutes
rules.inq.money.0: What was appropriated against what was authorized, and who ended up paying?
rules.inq.money.1: Dollar amounts by fiscal year and account; unfunded duties; who bore the cost
rules.inq.money.2: Appropriations acts and reports; CBO estimates; USAspending; GAO
rules.inq.delegation.0: What must an agency do before this takes effect, and has it done it?
rules.inq.delegation.1: Rulemakings by docket; standards bodies and their members; advisory panel rosters; time elapsed
rules.inq.delegation.2: Federal Register; regulations.gov; advisory committee records; ACUS studies
rules.inq.information.0: Who receives the information, is it public, and can anyone check it?
rules.inq.information.1: Reports filed and not filed; recipients; what was redacted; who audited
rules.inq.information.2: Committee sites; agency report pages; GAO; press comparison of promised and delivered disclosures
rules.inq.interaction.0: Which existing laws govern the same conduct, and which one prevails?
rules.inq.interaction.1: Sections by citation with the standard each applies; volume of use; which is specific and which is general
rules.inq.interaction.2: U.S. Code; CRS reports; case law on implied repeal and preemption
rules.inq.constitutional.0: Which doctrine has been used against provisions built like this one, and with what result?
rules.inq.constitutional.1: Cases with holdings; the feature of the provision that drew the challenge
rules.inq.constitutional.2: Constitution Annotated; Supreme Court and appellate opinions; CRS legal sidebars
rules.inq.symbolic.0: What happened to this text procedurally, and which binding vehicles exist or would be needed?
rules.inq.symbolic.1: Introductions, cosponsor counts, votes; companion bills and their status
rules.inq.symbolic.2: Congress.gov actions; roll call records; CRS on forms of legislation
rules.inq.evidence.0: Who measures compliance, with what data and baseline, and can the measured party shape the result?
rules.inq.evidence.1: Datasets, methods and thresholds; who supplies the data; known disputes about the measure
rules.inq.evidence.2: Agency methodology documents; GAO; academic critiques
rules.inq.market.0: Which firms fall on each side of each threshold, and who gains from the line?
rules.inq.market.1: Firms by name with size against the threshold; market shares; who sought the provision
rules.inq.market.2: Securities filings; FTC and agency studies; lobbying disclosures
rules.inq.process.0: How did the text change between versions, and who sought the change?
rules.inq.process.1: Version-to-version differences; amendments and sponsors; registered lobbying on the provision
rules.inq.process.2: Congress.gov text versions; Congressional Record; Lobbying Disclosure Act filings
rules.inq.mechanics.0: How have courts read a sentence built this way, and which reading helps whom?
rules.inq.mechanics.1: The competing readings in plain words; the canon each relies on; a decided case with the same sentence shape
rules.inq.mechanics.2: Supreme Court and appellate opinions; the CRS canon list; the House and Senate drafting manuals
rules.inq.response.0: What is the cheapest change in form, structure or timing that takes a regulated party outside this rule?
rules.inq.response.1: The specific restructuring, split, relabeling or substitute; who has already announced or used it
rules.inq.response.2: Law firm and accounting firm client alerts; trade press; agency notices closing or confirming a route; tax scholarship
rules.inq.design.0: Has a program built this way worked, and what did auditors find?
rules.inq.design.1: The comparable program; the audit finding; numbers for take-up, error or fraud
rules.inq.design.2: GAO and inspector general reports; implementation studies; state sunset reviews
rules.cand.0.1: Restructuring an activity so a lighter regime applies
rules.cand.1.1: Disputes over which legal category an actor falls in, such as employee, bank or broker
rules.cand.1.2: Tax Notes; labor and financial regulation case studies
rules.cand.2.1: Staying just under a size trigger, or splitting to do so
rules.cand.3.1: A statute that lets the agency waive the statute's own core requirements
rules.cand.4.1: Declining to enforce as a way of changing the law in practice
rules.cand.4.2: Inspector general reports; administrative law journals
rules.cand.5.1: Sunsets and phase-ins arranged to meet a cost estimate
rules.cand.6.1: Text enacted through omnibus or emergency measures with no committee process
rules.cand.7.1: Errors identified by outside experts while a bill is moving
rules.cand.8.1: Since 2024, courts and not agencies resolve statutory ambiguity, which changes what vague delegations do
rules.cand.9.1: The regulated agency helps draft its own constraints
rules.cand.10.1: Fee shifting, bounties and citizen suits, and their absence
rules.cand.11.1: Deadlines that carry an automatic consequence, and deadlines that do not
rules.cand.12.1: Drafting problems courts have formally reported to Congress
rules.mech.open_term.1: Breadth reaches actors, technologies and situations the drafters did not foresee. A list or tight definition can leave something out, and what is left out is presumed excluded.
rules.mech.open_term.2: Whoever applies the term first can choose the narrow reading. Disputes take years, and different courts can read it differently.
rules.mech.open_term.3: Who interprets the term first, and do they share the measure's purpose? Is the risk of leaving something out larger than the risk of a narrow reading?
rules.mech.discretion.1: Lets the official fit the rule to the facts, protect third parties case by case and avoid absurd mandatory results.
rules.mech.discretion.2: A reluctant official can decline to act, and no one can compel a choice the law left open.
rules.mech.discretion.3: Is the official holding the discretion one the measure relies on, or one it is aimed at?
rules.mech.feasibility.1: Avoids commanding the impossible and makes the provision harder to strike down.
rules.mech.feasibility.2: The standard is set by evidence about what is feasible, which usually comes from the regulated party.
rules.mech.feasibility.3: Who must prove what is feasible, and who checks the claim?
rules.mech.exception.1: Protects legitimate cases such as emergencies, victims and small actors, rewards good-faith compliance, and can be the price of passage.
rules.mech.exception.2: Exceptions grow. The party the rule constrains is usually the one invoking them.
rules.mech.exception.3: Who invokes it, is each use counted and reviewed, and does it expire?
rules.mech.threshold.1: Spares small actors and concentrates enforcement where the risk is.
rules.mech.threshold.2: Actors restructure to stay under the line, and a fixed line ages as markets and technology move.
rules.mech.threshold.3: How cheaply can someone split or restructure to get under it, and is the line indexed or aggregated?
rules.mech.timing.1: Gives time to comply, forces Congress to revisit an untested policy, and protects those who relied on the old rule.
rules.mech.timing.2: Delay can become repeal, a sunset creates a cliff others can exploit, and grandfathering entrenches incumbents.
rules.mech.timing.3: What happens by default when the date arrives and nobody acts?
rules.mech.delegation.0: Delegation to an agency or outside body
rules.mech.delegation.1: Brings expertise and lets the rule keep pace with change without new legislation.
rules.mech.delegation.2: The agency can delay or be captured, and since 2024 courts, not agencies, resolve statutory ambiguity.
rules.mech.delegation.3: Is there a deadline with a default rule if the agency does nothing, and who sits on the body?
rules.mech.remedy_limit.1: Prevents opportunistic lawsuits, keeps enforcement consistent and protects public funds.
rules.mech.remedy_limit.2: A right without a remedy depends on an enforcer who may lack resources, independence or interest.
rules.mech.remedy_limit.3: Does the body that can enforce have the means and the motive to do it?
rules.mech.narrow_scope.1: Easier to pass, clear about who is responsible, and less exposed to constitutional challenge.
rules.mech.narrow_scope.2: The activity or the records move to whoever is not covered.
rules.mech.narrow_scope.3: How easily can the conduct shift outside the scope?
rules.mech.preempt.1: One national rule lowers compliance cost and prevents conflicting obligations.
rules.mech.preempt.2: A federal floor can become a ceiling and displace stronger state protections.
rules.mech.preempt.3: Does it set a floor or a ceiling, and what state law does it displace today?
rules.mech.confidentiality.1: Protects victims, security and legitimate commercial secrets.
rules.mech.confidentiality.2: The same shield covers the conduct the measure is meant to expose.
rules.mech.confidentiality.3: Who reviews a claim of confidentiality, and can they see the material?
rules.mech.symbolic.1: Builds a record and a coalition, signals direction, and gathers evidence before a mandate.
rules.mech.symbolic.2: It can stand in for action and be presented as if something was done.
rules.mech.symbolic.3: Is there a binding companion, or a trigger that turns the study into a duty?
rules.mech.funding_flex.1: Keeps annual control over spending and lets funding track results.
rules.mech.funding_flex.2: A duty without money does not happen, and funding becomes a way to repeal quietly.
rules.mech.funding_flex.3: Is the duty conditioned on funding, and what happens in a year with none?
rules.mech.measurement.1: A simple measure can be administered and compared across cases.
rules.mech.measurement.2: The measured party learns to satisfy the metric without achieving the goal.
rules.mech.measurement.3: Who supplies the data, and can the method be changed without notice?
rules.standards.0.who: House Office of the Legislative Counsel
rules.standards.0.says: Use the present tense, singular and active voice, "may" for a power, "shall" for a duty and "may not" for a prohibition. Discourage findings and purposes (sec. 325), and a severability clause is unnecessary unless it says in detail which provisions fall (sec. 328).
rules.standards.1.who: House Office of the Legislative Counsel
rules.standards.1.says: States the inside-the-quotes rule for amendatory text and the rule on citing positive law titles.
rules.standards.2.who: House Office of the Legislative Counsel
rules.standards.2.says: A short guide of House drafting conventions, revised 10 June 2026.
rules.standards.3.who: House Office of the Legislative Counsel
rules.standards.3.says: Lists drafter's questions: to whom the policy applies, what exceptions exist, who carries it out, "What if the policy is not followed?", whether penalties are civil or criminal, how much lead time is needed, and whether transitional rules are required.
rules.standards.4.who: Senate Office of the Legislative Counsel
rules.standards.4.says: "'And/or' has not gained acceptance in legislative drafting" (sec. 302), and "Avoid the use of 'notwithstanding any other provision of law'" (sec. 314). A severability clause "is unnecessary" (sec. 131), and a sunset of authority does not repeal amendments the Act made (sec. 127).
rules.standards.5.who: Congress, codified by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel
rules.standards.5.says: Default meanings apply unless the context indicates otherwise: singular includes plural, present tense includes the future, and "person" includes corporations. Each section should contain, as nearly as may be, a single proposition of enactment, and a repealed Act is not revived by repeal of the repealer unless expressly provided.
rules.standards.6.who: Office of the Law Revision Counsel
rules.standards.6.says: Explains that a positive law title is amended directly while a non-positive title is amended through the underlying Act.
rules.standards.7.says: A committee report must print the text of each section to be repealed and "a comparative print of each amendment".
rules.standards.8.says: Contains the Cordon rule, requires a cost estimate and a regulatory impact evaluation in committee reports, bars general legislation on appropriations bills and confines conferees to matter committed to them.
rules.standards.9.who: U.S. Senate, as described by the Congressional Research Service
rules.standards.9.says: A reconciliation provision is extraneous on six grounds, including one that it "does not produce a change in outlays or revenues".
rules.standards.10.says: Agency legislative proposals must carry a section-by-section analysis and budget and personnel impacts, and backdoor financing is limited.
rules.standards.11.says: Covers executive agency documents only, excludes regulations and bars judicial review of compliance, so it does not reach bills.
rules.standards.13.says: Directs executive drafters to state limitations periods, preemptive effect, retroactivity, burdens of proof and key definitions in clear language.
rules.standards.14.says: "Do NOT use 'shall' or 'must' to state a rule of law" and "Do not include substantive provisions in a definition."
rules.standards.15.who: UK Office of the Parliamentary Counsel
rules.standards.15.says: Avoids the legislative "shall", warns against "sandwich" provisions and mixed conjunctions, and says to add "or both" where "or" is inclusive.
rules.standards.16.says: Bars circular and serial references, requires a static reference to say so, and bars autonomous substantive provisions inside amending acts.
rules.standards.17.says: Adds subject-specific directions on offences, regulatory powers, evidence and conferral of powers; only titles and dates were confirmed.
rules.conflicts.0.says: Include a clear severability clause (also add severability for litigation-friendly drafting).
rules.conflicts.0.but: Both manuals call a general severability clause unnecessary because courts presume severability; the better practice is a specific nonseverability clause or fallback for provisions that form a package.
rules.conflicts.0.src: Senate manual sec. 131; HOLC manual sec. 328
rules.conflicts.1.says: Add a rule that lists are illustrative, with "including but not limited to" as a cue.
rules.conflicts.1.but: Both manuals say "includes" already signals a partial list and "but is not limited to" is redundant; the risk they identify is "means" used where an open list was intended.
rules.conflicts.2.says: Include specific findings, specific findings on scope, and a statement that purposes guide interpretation.
rules.conflicts.2.but: HOLC manual sec. 325 says to discourage findings and purposes, though HOLC and the Senate manual accept findings that help establish congressional power or clarity, and the ADA has an enacted rule of construction.
rules.conflicts.3.but: Under TransUnion v. Ramirez, Congress may not relieve federal courts of deciding whether a plaintiff has a concrete harm, so a statutory grant of standing does not by itself open the federal courthouse.
rules.conflicts.4.says: Add meaningful penalties, enforcement funding and a private right of action.
rules.conflicts.4.but: CRS documents three limits: agency-tribunal civil penalties face the Jarkesy jury-trial holding, statutory damages without concrete harm face TransUnion, and spending-statute rights need rights-creating terms after Medina.
rules.conflicts.5.says: Rely on an independent regulator or assessor assumed to be insulated from removal.
rules.conflicts.5.but: CRS reports that Trump v. Slaughter (29 June 2026) overruled Humphrey's Executor and held FTC commissioners removable at will, with Federal Reserve governors treated separately.
rules.conflicts.6.says: Provide a dedicated funding source and pair authorizations with mandatory funding.
rules.conflicts.6.but: The CFPB episode shows the limit: the 2025 law cut the funding cap from 12 to 6.5 percent and the Bureau declined to request funds until a court ruled; OMB A-19 and the manuals also disagree on "such sums as may be necessary".
rules.conflicts.7.says: Add a default rule or a right to sue when a deadline is missed.
rules.conflicts.7.but: CRS describes such hammers as self-enforcing but warns of hastily imposed rules, and ACUS Recommendation 78-3 says Congress ordinarily should not impose statutory time limits on rulemaking.
rules.conflicts.8.says: Treat "reasonable" or "appropriate" as a weakness and give express discretion to the agency.
rules.conflicts.8.but: Loper Bright recognizes that a statute may expressly delegate definitional authority or leave agencies flexibility, citing enacted formulas such as "as such terms are defined and delimited by regulations of the Secretary".
